Today Apple officially released iOS 27.2 beta 1, skipping the 27.1 testing cycle. Among other changes, the new iOS 27.2 update also includes the previously announced brand-new Health app.

The all-new Apple Health app debuts in iOS 27.2 beta 1

Apple previewed last week at its September event a brand-new Health app coming to iPhone later this year.

And today, beta testers can get their first hands-on experience with the redesigned Health app via iOS 27.2 beta 1.

When Apple introduced the new Health app, it specifically highlighted how Apple Intelligence is used to help users better understand their own health. Here's what the company said:

Now in iOS 27.2 beta 1, if you're a developer, you can try out the two new tabs: "Insights" and "Longevity".

Since the new Health app relies on Apple Intelligence to operate, you'll need an AI-capable iPhone to use it. Some features also require pairing with an Apple Watch, and the device must be set to U.S. English.

So if your iPhone is less powerful than the iPhone 15 Pro, or you don't have a compatible Apple Watch, you won't be able to use these new Health app features. However, for other users, iOS 27.2 offers a first glimpse at Apple's vision for expanding the Health app.

Note: Apple says more health features will be added in subsequent beta versions, such as booking lab tests via Quest and providing personalized recommendations. Although the new Health app has already appeared in the beta, Apple says it won't be included in the official release of iOS 27.2, but will launch officially later this year.

What do you think of the changes to the Health app in iOS 27.2? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
